newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's tax plan may spark US backlash - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's tax plan may spark US backlash - paper.

text.p: U.S. corporations with stakes in UK regional electricity companies are lobbying U.S. politicians to retaliate against any move by a UK Labour government to impose a one-off tax on utilities, the Independent on Sunday reported.

Britain's opposition Labour Party, currently more than 25 percentage points ahead of the ruling Conservatives in opinion polls, plans a "windfall" tax on privatised utilities in order to raise at least three billion pounds ($4.8 billion) for job creation schemes.
If the U.S. power corporations are successful in seeking promises of counter-sanctions in Washington, British companies doing business in the U.S. could suffer, the newspaper said.
The paper said U.S. firms would call for legislation that would extract as much money from UK companies as the windfall tax would cost them.
Texas-based Central & South West Corporation, which owns Seeboard in the UK, is at the centre of the U.S. lobbying, the paper said.
In an interview on Sunday, Labour finance spokesman Gordon Brown declined to name specific companies which would be liable to pay the windfall tax.
"The companies that are affected and will be considered for this tax are those companies which have been privatised and are licensed and regulated by statute," Brown told the BBC.
"These are the companies that would be eligible but if they had not made excess profits they would not be liable."
Brown said the companies liable would be decided within the UK Treasury and the categories and rules governing the tax would be announced in Labour's first budget.
There has been speculation that companies such as British Telecom may be liable to pay the tax.
